newsitem.title: MEXICO: Latam stocks seen cautious over FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: Latam stocks seen cautious over FOMC meeting.

text.p: Investors can expect a cautious start to the week while Latin American bourses await the outcome of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rates.

In Mexico, many stockwatchers said a hike of 25 basis points in U.S. base rates would not cause lasting harm to share prices. "A rise in the Federal Funds rate could lead to some nervousness, but a hike in the discount rate would have little impact," said Gerardo Copca, associate research director at the Valores Finamex brokerage.

Other analysts were cautiously optimistic and said Mexican shares could head towards record levels at the end of the week. Last week, the blue chip IPC index inched up 0.44 percent to 3,890.36 points after a turbulent run on the back of Wall Street.
Argentine stocks were seen keeping a firm underlying tone but traders said their performance this week would hinge on the outcome of Tuesday's U.S. FOMC meeting.
"If the Fed notches up rates again we may see a downward correction on the bolsa, but this effect would be temporary," said Luis Corsiglia at brokers Corsiglia y Cia.
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 2.7 percent last week to an eight-week high of 743.03.
Traders said if the trend remained positive, the MerVal might overcome resistance at 750 and aim for the year's high of 760 in the near term.
Brazil stocks are seen rising cautiously this week as investors look to developments of an alleged vote-buying scandal involving a re-election bill and the U.S. FOMC meeting, brokers said.
Traders said worries eased over the alleged scam which erupted in the media last week as the threat of a broad congressional inquiry into the case appears to be vanishing.

But investors should have a cautious approach to stocks as investigations conducted by a lower house committee are not over yet. The Bovespa index of the 48 most active shares ended last week flat at 10,498 points.
Caracas blue chips were seen uncertain after profit-taking Friday dented a four day rally fueled by a slew of positive research recommendations and strong foreign bids, traders said.
"I'm still optimistic ... although the week's performance will depend largely on the fortunes of Wall Street," said Activalores broker Gustavo Alonso.
Last week, the Caracas bolsa's 19-share firmed 0.7 percent on the week to 6,632.21 points.
After losing ground last week, Chilean shares are seen steady with investors also waiting the outcome of Tuesday's FOMC meeting, traders said.
"The Chile market will remain well supported but the big issue next week will be how Latin America reacts to the Fed," said one trader.

Electricity stocks, which account for around a 40 percent weighting in the blue-chip index, are seen firming on hopes that heavy weekend rainfall will ease this year's drought, which has dried reservoirs in central and southern Chile.
The index ended last week down 0.62 percent at 119.85 points. Turnover was light all week with investors shying clear of the market as they awaited the FOMC meeting.
